item.title: Concept Modulation Models: A Unified Framework for Identifiability and Extrapolation
item.description: Concept modulation models connect identifiability and extrapolation in conditional generative models. Attributes determine modulators, which govern latent concepts and ultimately observed features. The framework uses attribute potentials to characterize both the latent transformations compatible with observed data and the conditions under which agreement extends to unseen attributes. This provides algebraic extrapolation criteria and a common basis for several existing results in nonlinear ICA, causal representation learning, and perturbation modeling.

item.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Brownian Motion Tree Models Based on One Sample
Context-Informed Ship Trajectory Prediction via Conditional Attention
item.description: The Conditional Informer predicts ship trajectories by conditioning vessel dynamics on environmental information. Its attention mechanism lets vessel states query contextual variables such as weather, reflecting the directional dependence of motion on environmental conditions. A modality masking strategy improves robustness when contextual sensors are unavailable. Experiments combining AIS trajectories with ERA5 weather data show improved forecasting accuracy and substantially reduced errors when context is missing.

item.title: Catastrophic Compositional Generation: Why Vanilla Diffusion Models Fail to Extrapolate
item.description: Compositional generation asks a conditional model to sample distributions defined by combinations of conditions beyond those observed during training. This work argues that vanilla conditional diffusion models can fail at this task even with improved inference-time procedures. Theory-guided arguments and experiments suggest that errors in learned scores can dominate sampling approximation errors for extrapolative targets, motivating approaches that address the underlying generalization problem.

item.title: A Unifying Framework for Unsupervised Concept Extraction
item.description: Concept extraction methods, including sparse autoencoders and transcoders, seek symbolic concepts within learned representations. This work studies their theoretical guarantees by treating concept extraction as a generative-model identification problem. A general identifiability theorem reduces the analysis to characterizing the intersection of two sets. Applying the framework to several common methods simplifies existing arguments and provides a foundation for designing concept extraction approaches with provable guarantees.

item.title: Causal Representation Learning
item.description: This chapter introduces causal representation learning as an inverse problem: recovering a latent causal model from the observations it generates. It reviews how interventions on latent variables can make this recovery possible, covering identifiability results for parametric and nonparametric models under interventions on one or multiple variables. The chapter also discusses practical algorithms that connect these theoretical results to representation learning.

DCI: Learning Causal Differences between Gene Regulatory Networks
item.description: Difference causal inference (DCI) identifies changes in gene regulatory relationships across two conditions directly from their expression data. Rather than reconstructing both complete networks, the algorithm estimates which causal edges appear, disappear, or change strength, reducing sample and computational requirements. A Python implementation includes stability selection across tuning parameters. Applications to single-cell RNA sequencing illustrate network comparison and validation through intervention-effect prediction.
